content:
Elliot Price: pulling together docs for the Optimization Suggestions beta. Need alignment on language so we’re not implying guaranteed savings. Current draft uses “estimated savings” but a few places still say “you’ll save”. Can folks sanity check preferred wording + where we want the Console to link?

Marissa Cole: +1 please be conservative. We had a few internal reviews flagging “save $X/day” as sounding contractual. In UI we’re showing “Estimated savings” with confidence and stale_as_of. Docs should mirror.

Aditya Rao: Agree. Recommend we standardize on:
- “estimated savings” / “estimated cost reduction”
- “based on the last N days of observed traffic”
- “actual costs may vary”
And explicitly: not a pricing commitment, not a guarantee.

Dev Patel: From Support side: please add a line about why billing might not match exactly (discounts, committed spend, rounding, different aggregation windows). We already have a ticket where customer compared estimate vs invoice.

Miguel Santos: From beta calls, the phrase that lands best is “directionally correct; validate via rollout”. Also folks ask “is risk security?” so docs should repeat “risk here = performance/reliability risk” not security/compliance.

Tessa Morgan: Copy suggestion (matches the drawer tone):
“Estimated savings are projections, not guarantees. We compute estimates from recent usage and modeled changes to batching/caching. Real-world results vary based on traffic shape, model behavior, and your pricing terms.”
Also avoid absolute language like “will” / “ensures”.

Jean-Paul Laurent: For in-product education: we should keep the disclaimer short in Console, then link to longer doc.
Proposed Console microcopy (banner or footer):
“Estimates are based on recent traffic and may differ from billed amounts. Learn how we calculate estimates.”

Elliot Price: ok. Two concrete questions:
1) Do we want “not a guarantee” sentence on the docs page top, or only in an FAQ?
2) Where exactly in Console do we link: Suggestions list header, details drawer, or both?

Marissa Cole: 1) Put it near the top (first screen), not buried.
2) Both.
- List page: small info callout near “Estimated savings” column header (or above table).
- Details drawer: “How we estimate this” link right under the estimate + confidence.

Aditya Rao: +1. Also add “Beta limitation” note: only batching/caching suggestions; quantization is out of scope for this view.

Nadia Rahman: Please include a sentence on the aggregation window + staleness. Something like:
“Estimates use the last 7 days of telemetry when available. If telemetry is delayed, the estimate may be stale; check the ‘as of’ timestamp.”
We’ve seen pipeline lag in a couple orgs.

Dev Patel: Also add a troubleshooting bullet: “If estimate seems high/low: confirm telemetry enabled, check traffic recently changed, verify you’re looking at same route/project, and compare to usage not invoice.” Helps reduce back-and-forth.

Elliot Price: Drafting updated language now. Proposed top-of-page disclaimer block:
- “Savings are estimates, not guarantees.”
- “Estimates are derived from recent usage telemetry and modeled changes to batching/caching.”
- “Billed amounts may differ due to pricing terms (discounts/commits), aggregation windows, and traffic variability.”
- “Recommendations are not automatically applied; use rollouts/canaries to validate.”
Any red flags?

Tessa Morgan: Looks good. Minor: “modeled changes” can read scary—maybe “simulated” or “projected under expected traffic”.

Jean-Paul Laurent: +1 change “modeled” -> “projected”. Also suggest we define “confidence” in one line: “Confidence reflects the quality/coverage of telemetry inputs, not a guarantee of outcome.”

Marissa Cole: Yes on confidence clarification. Also make sure we say “risk level reflects likelihood of latency/reliability impact” (not quality, unless we explicitly mean it). For beta I’d keep it performance/reliability only.

Aditya Rao: Agree. Keep quality out for now.

Elliot Price: Cool. For linking: I’ll ask Nora/Console team to add link targets. For docs URL, I’m planning:
/console/optimize/optimization-suggestions-beta#how-estimates-work
and #limitations + #troubleshooting anchors. Sound ok?

Dev Patel: Works. If you can, add a short “What this is not” section:
- not a promise
- not a contract amendment
- not a billing reconciliation tool
We can point customers there.

Miguel Santos: +1. Also include “validate with a staged rollout” section with 3 steps (apply to a canary route/project, monitor p95 + error rate, then expand).

Elliot Price: done. I’ll update draft + ping when PR is up. Thanks all.
